newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Copper stocks seen posting small rise - trade.
newsitem.headline: Copper stocks seen posting small rise - trade.

text.p: Far East metal traders said on Tuesday London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks would probably rise by about 2,000-3,000 tonnes with trading seen extremely quiet the day before Christmas.
Aluminium stocks, on the other hand, will slide by about 1,000-2,000 tonnes after rising by 6,350 tonnes in the last LME report on Friday, the dealers said.

"We should see copper stocks go up 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading firm said. "But everything is really very quiet and we don't expect any substantial activity this afternoon."
Another dealer said most people in the market were more concerned about leaving their offices early for the Christmas Day holiday.
"Nobody wants to talk about stocks today. The only thing people are talking about is what time they're going home," a dealer for a European metal trading company said.
The amount of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse may show a small increase, traders said.
Copper stocks in the LME's warehouse here reached 24,950 tonnes last Friday, up 1,200 tonnes from last Tuesday and from only 1,975 tonnes at the end of September.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at around US$2,125/30 a tonne at 0200 GMT, almost unchanged from the late trade in London on Monday of $2,126/28 a tonne.
Cash copper was quoted at around $2,224/29 a tonne with backwardation seen at $99 a tonne.
Three month aluminium prices were seen at 0200 GMT at $1,552/57 a tonne against the last quote in London yesterday of $1,552/54 a tonne, dealers said.
